definitions.terms: In every test a character is one UTF-16 unit of the JavaScript string (every route here holds only characters of 16 bits). The text is the whole route text as it stands, the field route of a line of the by-source JSONL, what the checker gives the classifier, and never the field def. Nothing is trimmed unless a test says so. What the bracket holds means, for a round bracket, the characters between that opener and its closer, nothing added and nothing taken away, spaces included: the template's c.group. The text before the mark means every character from the start of the text up to, and not including, the mark. Whitespace at the end taken off means the JavaScript trimEnd of the string. Begins with the string means that the string's characters are exactly the first characters of the text, with nothing before them. Is one of the strings in a list means is equal to one string of that list, character for character and whole. Every string and every list minds case. A string stands between « and », which are not part of it. Inside round brackets means the template's container paren: the innermost bracket round the mark is a round bracket; the text inside those brackets is the template's c.inner.

branches.question: One row gives two names for one place of the text, with a comma between them: Samgar, Nebu-sar-sekim. The second name is made with the letters of the word that follows in the text. Today the page prints the row whole, as one pill. Does the comma divide, so that each name is a reading of its own?

options.means: The comma does not cut: the page prints Samgar, Nebu-sar-sekim as one reading, as written, as it does today.
The comma cuts: the page prints Samgar and Nebu-sar-sekim as two readings.

Should the page print the name in both forms instead, Baal-hermon and Mount Baal-hermon, as two readings? That needs one step of the page's own, since the store's text does not change.
